params.text: The Suez Canal. A quiet history, read slowly, for sleep. The canal runs through Egypt, connecting the Mediterranean Sea in the north to the Red Sea in the south. It opened in eighteen sixty-nine, after roughly ten years of construction. Before it existed, ships travelling between Europe and Asia sailed around the southern tip of Africa, a far longer journey. The canal has no locks. The seas at either end sit at broadly similar levels, so water passes along its length without the stepped chambers used on many other canals. It has been widened and deepened many times since it opened, as ships have grown larger. Today it remains one of the busiest shipping routes in the world. Rest now. The rain will continue.
